chapters.title: Why SiteLight?
chapters.description: Compare lunar sites and mission dates in one workspace. See sunlight and Earth visibility.
chapters.use: Useful when a schedule changes and you need to reassess a site.

chapters.title: Two independent scenarios
chapters.description: Mission A and B hold separate sites and start times. Begin by selecting B, the Nobile study point.
chapters.use: Use the same requirements to compare choices fairly.

chapters.title: Set mission requirements
chapters.description: Choose the site, UTC start and duration. Here we require 70% sunlight, 90% Earth visibility and 70% overlap.
chapters.use: Apply settings evaluates the draft before replacing the current result.

chapters.title: Moon and terrain views
chapters.description: Moon shows the wider location. Terrain offers a cinematic view and a separate measured Source DEM.
chapters.use: Use Source DEM for the selected elevation grid. Cinematic landforms are illustrative.

chapters.title: Horizon and time lanes
chapters.description: The horizon plot places the Sun and Earth against surrounding terrain. Scrub time or play the timeline.
chapters.use: The Sun, Earth and Overlap lanes show when the selected conditions are available.

chapters.title: Compare the actual results
chapters.description: Compare keeps both scenarios under shared requirements. Read the sunlight, Earth and overlap values side by side.
chapters.use: For this setup: A sunlight 0%. B sunlight 73.1%, Earth 100%, overlap 73.1%.

chapters.title: Test a different start
chapters.description: Schedule scans loaded records for this site and these requirements. Preview a tested start, then apply it.
chapters.use: Preview keeps the baseline unchanged. Apply tested start rechecks it before updating the mission.

chapters.title: Inspect the ground
chapters.description: Terrain shows slope, roughness and coverage. Switch to Source DEM for measured elevation.
chapters.use: A footprint or sampled route provides screening evidence. Landing safety needs further assessment.

chapters.title: Replay Apollo evidence
chapters.description: Seismic adds historical catalogs and real archived impact waveforms. Replay the record and inspect its source.
chapters.use: Normalized waveforms explain historical observations. They do not predict local shaking or future events.

chapters.title: Thermal and dust context
chapters.description: View historical Diviner observations. Update sensitivity to explore assumed dust coverage.
chapters.use: Historical data provide context. Dust sensitivity remains an exploratory model.

chapters.title: Logistics trade-offs
chapters.description: Explore assumed ice and budget inputs beside a published NASA water-ISRU reference.
chapters.use: Ice and equipment choices are hypothetical. The reference study stays separate.

chapters.title: Trace and export evidence
chapters.description: Evidence links layers to their sources, validation and limits. Export keeps settings, results and qualifications together.
chapters.use: Use JSON for full evidence, CSV for time records, or Print / PDF for a review copy.

chapters.title: Your next comparison
chapters.description: Start another comparison in Explore. Set your requirements, compare the results and inspect the evidence.
chapters.use: Prepared real records. On-demand science needs a backend. Scientific acceptance remains open.
